title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). The page belongs to the 'variations on the loop equation' (équation des lacets), Grothendieck's analysis of how the Galois/GT-type automorphisms act on the profinite modular group. The model is 𝔖 = 𝔖_{0,3}^{+∧}, i.e. PSL(2,Ẑ) ≅ Ẑ/2 ∗ Ẑ/3 or a quotient of it. In it, ρ has order 3 and σ has order 2, ε_1 is the 'parabolic' generator (essentially ρσ up to convention), and L_1 = closure of ⟨ε_1⟩. 𝔊 is the group in question and 𝔊^∨ (or 𝔊') is a characteristic subgroup, the analogue of the commutator subgroup F̂_2' where the f of a GT pair lives. 𝔊_{ρ,σ} is a larger group in which 𝔊 is normal, and G_{ρ,σ} is the group introduced on the previous pages. Σ_{ρ,σ} is the set of pairs (ξ,η) of the shape below, and B_{ρ,σ} is an extension of Γ_{ρ,σ} by L_0; the previous page shows B_{ρ,σ} ≃ Σ_{ρ,σ}.

What the page does.
(27) It defines SG_{ρ,σ} as the set of pairs (α,β), α ∈ 𝔊^∨ and β ∈ 𝔊, such that ξ := αρ(α)^{-1} and η := βσ(β)^{-1} satisfy ξ = η·ε_1^ν for some ν ∈ Ẑ, i.e. η^{-1}ξ ∈ L_1. Here ρ(α) = ραρ^{-1}, so ξ = [α,ρ] and η = [β,σ] (written on the next page as αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1} = α(ρ)ρ^{-1}).
- In plain terms, (α,β) are the 'conjugating elements' of an automorphism that sends ρ ↦ αρα^{-1} and σ ↦ βσβ^{-1}.
- The condition says the two conjugates are compatible modulo the inertia L_1 generated by ε_1.
- This is exactly the shape of the Ihara–Drinfeld description of the Galois action on π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}) and of GT, transported to the orbifold group Ẑ/2 ∗ Ẑ/3 (the M_{1,1} level).

(28) The map (α,β) ↦ (ξ,η), from SG_{ρ,σ} to Σ_{ρ,σ}, is surjective by definition of Σ_{ρ,σ}. Hypothesis (10) supplies canonical sections (ξ,η) ↦ u_{ξ,η}. However, u_{ξ,η} lies only in 𝔊_{ρ,σ}, not in 𝔊.

(29) He therefore enlarges to 𝒢_{ρ,σ} ⊂ 𝔊_{ρ,σ} × 𝔊_{ρ,σ}, defined by the same equation.

(30) SG_{ρ,σ} = 𝒢_{ρ,σ} ∩ (𝔊^∨ × 𝔊).

NB in the margin: ξ = α(ρ)ρ^{-1} and η = β(σ)σ^{-1}, so ξ,η lie in 𝔊^∨ because 𝔊 is invariant in 𝔊_{ρ,σ}.

Where it leads. On the next page this becomes a structure theorem: G_{ρ,σ} ≅ B_{ρ,σ} × T_ρ × T_σ via (u,a,b) ↦ (ua^{-1}, ub^{-1}), with T_ρ and T_σ the centralisers of ρ and σ. This is a torsor-type parametrisation of all solutions of the loop equation, given a canonical solution u_{ξ,η}. The page itself is preparatory bookkeeping: definitions, a surjection, and the observation that the canonical section forces the passage to the enlarged group.
errors: The marginal NB is too quick. From 𝔊 normal in 𝔊_{ρ,σ} one gets ξ = αρα^{-1}ρ^{-1} ∈ 𝔊. Concluding ξ ∈ 𝔊^∨ (derived/characteristic subgroup) additionally requires that conjugation by α act trivially on the relevant quotient 𝔊/𝔊^∨ (e.g. the abelianisation). This is not stated on the page and is presumably part of the definition of 𝔊_{ρ,σ}.
Notational drift: (27) restricts α to 𝔊^∨ but β only to 𝔊. In (29) both are in 𝔊_{ρ,σ}. The asymmetry is deliberate (normalisation on one side, as for f ∈ F̂_2') but is not explained here.

The sentence introducing the canonical sections is incomplete and corrected ('par construction' crossed out, replaced by 'par définition'; 'certaines' crossed out). So the exact use of hypothesis (10) cannot be read off this page.

ideas.what: Parametrising automorphisms of a profinite group generated by torsion elements ρ (order 3) and σ (order 2) by pairs of conjugators (α,β) whose commutators [α,ρ] and [β,σ] agree modulo the parabolic subgroup L_1 = ⟨ε_1⟩
ideas.modern_name: Loop/hexagon-type equations for GT acting on PSL2(Ẑ) / the M_{1,1} level of the Teichmüller tower (cf. GT's action on Ẑ/2 ∗ Ẑ/3, the Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps 'new version' of GT)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara and Drinfeld (GT, ~1990); Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps and Lochak–Schneps for the M_{1,1}/PSL2 version (1997)
ideas.where_published: Motivating ideas in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) on the Teichmüller tower at levels (0,3),(1,1); the detailed computations appear only in these Longue Marche continuation notes

ideas.what: Canonical section Σ_{ρ,σ} → solution set, (ξ,η) ↦ u_{ξ,η}, forcing passage to an enlarged ambient group 𝔊_{ρ,σ}
ideas.modern_name: Splitting of the commutator map / choosing a base solution of a torsor
Normalised solutions as a slice of the full solution set

missed.claim: The page is a step in an apparently systematic treatment of the loop equation for an abstract profinite quotient 𝔖 of Ẑ/2 ∗ Ẑ/3. Here the solution set is organised as a torsor (B_{ρ,σ} × centralisers) over the commutator data Σ_{ρ,σ}. It does not seem to have been carried out at this generality in print, where most work is specific to F̂_2 or PSL2(Ẑ). The page itself contains only definitions.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A general framework for 'GT-type' groups attached to quotients of the modular group (finite-level or congruence quotients) is of interest for dessins d'enfants and Galois actions on modular towers. These notes could show how Grothendieck intended such groups to be defined.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly routine definitional bookkeeping. Its interest comes from context: Grothendieck's unpublished development of GT-type loop equations for the PSL2/M_{1,1} level, which is related to (but predates or parallels) published work by Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps. Nothing on this page itself is a new result.
transcription_corrections: In (27) the first factor looks like 𝔊^∨ (check superscript, consistent with 𝔖^∨ on the previous page) rather than 𝔊'. The relation symbol written over a crossed-out passage reads as '=' / '⊂' and is ambiguous.
'(sans rappeler (18) pour simplifier)' is more plausibly '(sans rappeler (ρ,σ) pour simplifier)', i.e. dropping the subscripts ρ,σ.
'et on fait par l'hypothèse (10) ... puisque' probably reads 'et on a, par l'hypothèse (10), des sections canoniques'; 'certaines' is crossed out.
In (29), 'pour un Ẑ conv.' should read 'pour un ν ∈ Ẑ convenable'.
In (29), η is written below βσ(β)^{-1} with a crossed-out symbol next to it, mirroring (27).
